subject: Inference edge trust zones and red-team findings
messages:
From: OpsSec Red Team <redteam@stratussec.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Red-team debrief: inference-edge trust zone exercise

Ben —

Thanks for hosting our exercise last week. Attached is the raw evidence capture and an executive summary. We ran a blast-radius simulation focused on the inference edge: sidecar egress pathways, control plane to data plane demarcation, and KV/cache persistence. High level findings:

- A permissive egress rule on a sidecar subnet allowed simulated exfiltration of cached model shards via a tunnel to a disposable endpoint.
- Control-plane API keys reused across staging and prod simulation led to privilege escalation in our scenario (we used a stolen CI token pattern).
- Lack of mTLS between some sidecar-hop pairs made man-in-the-middle replay trivial for the test harness.

We include suggested mitigations in the summary but wanted to highlight immediate, high-impact recommendations: egress allowlist enforcement at the elastic edge, shorter token TTLs + ephemeral session credentials for worker pods, and sealing model KV caches in an encrypted local-only store.

Files attached: rt-raw-evidence.pcap (pcap capture), stratus-redteam-exec-summary.pdf (3 pages).

Happy to walk through the packet traces with your infra team — available Tuesday/Wednesday.

— OpsSec Red Team

Next steps from our side:
- Kimberly: will own triage of the egress rule and close the open allowlist holes (INF-4321).
- Lauren: please coordinate a joint packet review session with OpsSec to validate the remediation once we apply the ACLs.
- Vanessa: verify that the dedicated control-plane HSM boundaries were not used in the test and file an attestation if clean.

OpsSec, we'd like a short walkthrough Tuesday at 10am PT if that works.

Ben

Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Red-team debrief: inference-edge trust zone exercise

Team — copying the exec summary and the diagram. Quick read: the vector exploited an egress rule attached to the inference sidecar subnet that allowed outbound connections to ephemeral IPs. The red team used a staged token to proxy requests and pull partial KV shards from the model cache.

Proposed remediation plan (short window, high impact):
1) Immediate: apply egress allowlist policy to all inference sidecar subnets (INF-4321). Block unknown outbound CIDR ranges.  
2) Short term (48–72h): rotate all staging/prod control-plane tokens to ephemeral sessions (SEC-214). Enforce per-service token scopes and reduce TTLs to <=10m for worker sessions.
3) Medium term (2 weeks): encrypt KV cache at rest with node-local keys sealed to the TPM/HSM and restrict any replication to an internal-only control channel.
4) Longer term: mTLS mandatory between sidecar hops; add eBPF-based egress filtering to detect protocol anomalies and drop tunneled exfil attempts.

Action items & owners:  
- Kimberly: patch egress ACLs + roll policy out to canary (INF-4321) — target: 24h
- Lauren: schedule packet review with OpsSec and product testing — target: 48h
- Vanessa: verify control-plane HSM boundaries and produce attestation doc — target: 72h
- Ben: raise a customer notification (sanitized) for Stratus Financial and coordinate legal review — target: today EOD

I started JIRA tickets and linked the drive folder. Send quick status updates to this thread.

Ben / team —

Quick updates: I patched the egress ACL on the canary subnet and rolled the policy to one additional cluster (policy id: egress-allow-2026-08-17). Initial telemetry shows no outbound attempts to the flagged ephemeral ranges. I created JIRA-INF-4321 with a checklist (apply to all regions, test harness, QA signoff).

Lauren: I added you to the packet review invite with OpsSec on Tue 10am PT. Vanessa: please upload the HSM attestation to the drive link and set the sharing to restricted for the Stratus legal contact.

Also moving SEC-214 into the critical lane — working with infra to set token TTLs and enable ephemeral sessions for pod workers. Will update this thread after the full rotate completes.

Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Infrastructure Security Engineer
Redwood Inference
